classification.difficultyReason: Undo the external multiplier and square root to isolate length, substitute the given period and gravity, then convert metres to centimetres before rounding.

content.prompt: The time $T$ (in seconds) taken for one complete swing of a pendulum is given by $T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$, where $g=9.8$ and $L$ is the length of the pendulum in metres. Find, correct to the nearest centimetre, the length of a pendulum that takes 2 seconds to complete one swing.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{T}{2\pi}&=\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}\\\frac{T^2}{4\pi^2}&=\frac{L}{g}\\L&=\frac{gT^2}{4\pi^2}\\L&=\frac{9.8\times2^2}{4\pi^2}\\L&=\frac{9.8}{\pi^2}\text{ m}\\L&=\frac{980}{\pi^2}\text{ cm}\\L&\approx99\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The length is $99\text{ cm}$, correct to the nearest centimetre.
